title: Sales are not profit
principle: Sales are not profit. Profit is what's left.

screens.text: Meena sold ₹2 lakh of sarees at the Diwali mela. She came home with almost nothing.

screens.prompt: Why did Meena make so little?

options.label: Her costs ate most of the sales

screens.why: She spent ₹1.9 lakh on stock, the stall and travel. Only ₹10,000 was left.

screens.title: The rule
screens.text: Sales are the money that comes in. Profit is what is left after you pay every cost.

screens.prompt: Sales ₹500. Costs ₹350. What is the profit?

wrong.a: ₹500 is the sales. You still have to pay the costs.
wrong.b: Costs come off the sales. They don't add to it.

screens.text: Profit is what is ___ after you pay every ___.
screens.why: Profit is what stays with you once every cost is paid.

screens.prompt: Ravi says: "I sold ₹1 lakh this month, so I made ₹1 lakh." Is he right?

options.label: Yes, sales are what you make
No, he must take off his costs

screens.why: ₹1 lakh is his sales. His profit is that minus rent, stock and wages.

screens.setup: You run a tea stall. A bigger stall nearby sells twice as many cups as you.
screens.question: Your friend says you should copy them. What do you ask first?

options.label: How much do they keep from each cup?
options.outcome: You learn they sell cheap and keep ₹1 a cup. You keep ₹4. You stay as you are.
options.why: Big sales mean nothing until you know the costs.

options.label: Where do they buy their cups?
options.outcome: You find a cheaper cup supplier, but you still don't know if they make money.
options.why: Cheaper cups help a little, but you skipped the big question.
options.better: First ask how much they keep from each cup.

options.label: Nothing. Just cut your price to match
options.outcome: You sell more cups and make less money than before.
options.why: You copied their sales, not their profit.
options.better: Find out what they keep from each cup before you change anything.

summary: Sales are the money that comes in.
Profit is what is left after every cost.

cards.front: A stall sells ₹10,000 in a day and spends ₹9,000. What is its profit?
"We sold a lot, so we made a lot." True?
cards.back: Not always. High sales with high costs can leave nothing.
